hn-50212065.t: Kimi K3.1 Pro and K3.1 Pro Highspeed
hn-50212065.s: Introducing Kimi K3.1 Pro, our most capable 3T-class open-weight model with 1M-token context and major advances in coding, 3D modeling, and financial research.
ex: We're introducing Kimi K3.1 Pro, the first model in our new K3.1 series and our most capable 3T-class open-weight model to date, with a 1-million-token context window. It delivers substantial improvements across coding, 3D creation, financial research, and other agentic capabilities. We are also releasing Kimi K3.1 Pro Highspeed, which delivers 2-3× the speed of K3.1 Pro for more responsive interactions. Kimi K3.1 Pro and Kimi K3.1 Pro Highspeed are available today on Kimi.ai, Kimi Work, Kimi Code, and the Kimi API. The full model weights will be released by Nov 4. Kimi K3.1 Pro is a post-trained version of Kimi K3, with substantially larger post-training compute.

hn-50214218.t: Now Google says it might use your Gmail and Google Photos data to target ads
hn-50214218.s: According to the new terms, sharing your data for better AI recommendations also means opening it up for more personalized ads.
ex: According to the new terms, sharing your data for better AI recommendations also means opening it up for more personalized ads. According to the new terms, sharing your data for better AI recommendations also means opening it up for more personalized ads. That means anyone who has connected their Drive, Gmail, or Google Photos to AI Mode and other Search tools via Google’s Personal Intelligence feature — allowing those tools to provide better responses or recommendations by knowing more about you — may now see ads targeted on the basis of that content. Advertisers don’t get access to your Drive, Gmail, and Photos information or personally identifying details such as your name or email address, and Google won’t show you ads based on sensitive categories like race, sexual orientation, religion, or health.

hn-50202217.t: LLMs are making formal software verification feasible at a much larger scale
hn-50202217.s: Claude formally proved security properties in the compiled code of 123 open-source libraries. Along the way, it found bugs that had eluded detection for years.
ex: Keane Lucas, Aengus Lynch, Luna Tong, Luke Champine, Zygi Straznickas, Dino Distefano, Harshikaa AgrawalEvyatar Ben Asher, Ava Howell, Sami Jawhar, Chris Rohlf, Nickolai ZeldovichNicholas Carlini, Rajashree Agrawal, Jason Gross Most software is riddled with bugs, which AI can now easily find and exploit. The standard defenses against cyberattacks are no longer sufficient: we need ways to prove that code is free of bugs. Formal software verification could provide this guarantee, but it has historically required years of expert effort, making it impractical for most real-world projects. In a collaboration with Theorem, however, we show this is no longer the case: LLMs can now produce formal proofs at large scale, enabling new software development workflows that include proven security guarantees. Using Claude, we proved security properties at the assembly code level (RISC-V) in over 100 real-world open-source software libraries.

hn-50213925.t: Dessa: the most authentic full-duplex speech model ever built
hn-50213925.s: You learned to talk by listening. So did Dessa. A research preview of a full-duplex speech model.
ex: We believe voice is the most natural way to interact with intelligence, so we created Dessa, the most authentic full-duplex speech model ever built. Talking with it feels like talking with a person…full of emotion, nuance, pauses, and a natural cadence. Interacting with current voice AI can just plain suck. It turns your voice into text and throws away an incredible amount of information text alone can’t carry. The most powerful AIs in the world can’t hear how you feel. We think that’s ridiculous, leads to a worse experience, and is potentially dangerous. We trained Dessa from scratch on nothing but human conversation. Sounds! No text, no pretrained models. It learned to hold a real-time conversation simply by listening. As far as we know, Dessa is the world’s first AI you can have a realistic live conversation with that was trained only from human speech.

hn-50195488.t: OnKey – I'm a bad singer, so I built an app to show where I'm off-key
hn-50195488.s: Learn to sing the songs you love. A free, open-source singing trainer for Mac that listens to the music you play.
ex: OnKey is a free, open-source singing trainer for the Mac. Play a song in Spotify, Apple Music, or YouTube in a browser, and sing along. The first time, you get the lyrics, and OnKey learns the singer's melody when the song ends. After that, the notes scroll towards you, your pitch is drawn over them, and you get a score with a report on every line. OnKey doesn't provide, stream or download music. Your own music app plays it. You need a Mac with Apple Silicon (M1 or later) and macOS 14.2 or later. Download OnKey.dmg (from the latest release), open it and drag OnKey to Applications. Setup asks for the microphone, to hear you, and for system audio recording, to hear the music app. It also asks whether OnKey may follow Spotify and Apple Music: choose Listen only and it follows songs by their sound alone. Getting started walks through it, and the FAQ answers the usual questions.

hn-50196837.t: Google cleared 300 hectares of Finnish forest
hn-50196837.s: Cutting corners: Google recently announced a major expansion of its data center footprint in Finland. The US company plans to invest billions in the new infrastructure but is allegedly moving a bit…
ex: Cutting corners: Google recently announced a major expansion of its data center footprint in Finland. The US company plans to invest billions in the new infrastructure but is allegedly moving a bit too quickly with its forest-clearing plans. Regulators are now looking into the matter, and the outcome could have far-reaching consequences for the broader market. Google was apparently so eager to build its new data center infrastructure in Finland that it began bulldozing large swaths of forest before the required environmental review of the full plan was complete. The work could now be suspended, just as other major data center projects are being delayed in the US and elsewhere around the world. The issue surfaced last month, when Finland's Permit and Supervision Agency (Lupa- ja valvontavirasto, or LVV) asked Tuike Finland Oy (TFO) to explain its actions.

hn-50208258.t: Hacker leaks 281 GB of data from Germany's far-right AfD party
hn-50208258.s: Germany's far-right AfD (Alternative für Deutschland) party has confirmed that it has suffered a security breach, after a hacker published what appear to be hundreds of thousands of the controversial…
ex: Germany's far-right AfD (Alternative für Deutschland) party has confirmed that it has suffered a security breach, after a hacker published what appear to be hundreds of thousands of the controversial political party's internal emails. Earlier this week, the AfD admitted that its hosting provider had been hacked in September, and that some of its mailboxes had been copied. The party claims that most of the affected mailboxes had not been used for years, but the leaked archive reportedly includes messages dated as recently as 12 September 2026. The news came as the Hexane.cc leak site published AI-written summaries of hundreds of thousands of the messages into categories such as racism and antisemitism, graded Low to Critical, according to local media reports. To add to the AfD's discomfort, reports suggest that the hacker's access may have been gained in an embarrassingly simple fashion, via a website that had allegedly been left unpatched.

hn-50207620.t: We had AI write a wiki from 45k Enron emails, every fact cited
hn-50207620.s: We gave an AI 45,047 of Enron's emails, and it wrote 214 pages about the companies, regulators and banks Enron dealt with. Every fact cites the email it came from.
ex: We gave an AI 45,047 of Enron's emails, and it wrote 214 pages about the companies, regulators and banks Enron dealt with. Every fact cites the email it came from. When the mail shows a fact stopped being true, the page expires it on that date. No one edited a page or a fact. The last two come from a held-out audit by a second AI; see how we checked it. These are the most-discussed organizations in the corpus. Each page has a slider. Drag it and the page shows what was known on that date, with facts that were only true for a while expiring in front of you. Facts on these pages are sentences, each with a date and a source, rather than fields like headcount or revenue. Fields belong in a CRM or another system of record, and a brain like this one sits beside it, holding what changes too often or doesn't fit in a field. We describe the three kinds of company knowledge, and where each one lives, in The missing middle of company knowledge.

hn-50202865.t: Making a smart TV dumb and then smart
hn-50202865.s: Local home screen, private remote browser, and push-to-talk voice assistant for webOS TVs
ex: Demo: https://anubhavmalhotra.com/vibing/r2d2-webos/r2d2-demo.mp4 Read the story behind the project: R2D2 for webOS. A local home screen, private remote browser, and push-to-talk voice assistant for webOS TVs. A Linux compute host runs Chromium and the voice models; the TV provides the display, applications, and remote control. - The keyfilter patch, Home/idle routing, and native voice capture replace or hook vendor services. A mistake can disable the remote, Home, or voice until the TV is restored. - Firmware SHA-256 pins, code offsets, symbol names, and patch anchors target one reference build. hn-50205934.t: Disney Raising Prices Days After Confirming Ads Will Now Show Up on Every Tier
hn-50205934.s: Disney+ is conspicuously absent from that list, which is worth highlighting given the streamer’s size and the fact that it has aired shows like Percy Jackson and Daredevil: Born Again.
ex: Twice a year, Nielsen pulls back the curtain on what America has actually been watching, and the numbers for the first-half of 2026 were revealed recently. It is a genuinely encouraging picture for streaming overall: Stranger Things and The Pitt are duking it out at the top, shows like One Piece, Invincible and Shrinking are pulling healthy numbers and cracking the Top 20 Most-Watched Originals, and kids remain the single biggest force in the ecosystem, with Bluey outpacing Grey’s Anatomy outright. Even The Big Bang Theory is having a bit of a renaissance. Streaming, in other words, is working.

hn-50195873.t: MPs moving to restrict gambling ads in Canada
hn-50195873.s: A new analysis for CBC News shows Canadians continue to be bombarded with betting promotions during sports broadcasts.
ex: This story is part of a CBC News series examining the public health impacts of online gambling. For T.S., a 22-year-old Ontario man recovering from a gambling problem, widespread advertising for online casinos and betting during sports broadcasts is "frustrating." "Imagine you're an alcoholic and there was a beer ad during every show you watched," he told CBC News. His gambling started three years ago as a fun Friday night activity with friends, but escalated. One night last year he found himself locked inside a bathroom, losing it all — having bet away $14,000. T.S., who CBC has agreed not to name, says he quickly sought treatment and hasn't gambled since. But during his spree, all those ads fuelled him to gamble more. "It certainly … would trigger me to go back and place another bet." Politicians in Ottawa are moving to curb the widespread advertising currently seen across sports broadcasts, social media and online video games. Sports gambling ads are everywhere.

hn-50202114.t: Canadians are running out of time to oppose Bill C-22
hn-50202114.s: Canada’s Parliament is debating a massive expansion of surveillance powers that will threaten the privacy and security of millions of people.
ex: Canada’s Parliament is debating a massive expansion of surveillance powers that will threaten the privacy and security of millions of people. Bill C-22, also called the Lawful Access Act, has already passed the House of Commons, and is now before the Canadian Senate. Canadians still have an opportunity to speak out and stop this dangerous legislation. The Canadian Civil Liberties Association (CCLA) is urging all Canadians to sign its petition opposing the bill. (The petition on CCLA’s website is governed by CCLA’s privacy policy.) As we wrote earlier this year, Bill C-22 gives the government new powers to force digital services—including telecom companies, messaging apps, and more—to help with government surveillance. Worse, it allows Canada’s Minister of Public Safety to order companies to create a backdoor to their services for law enforcement, as long as it doesn’t lead to a “systemic insecurity.” That’s a clear recipe for weakening the encryption we all rely on.
